sub: From the written code of DNA to a world of creatures that complete one another, eight units reveal how life everywhere speaks of the Lord who gives life.

units.title: DNA: The Language of Life
units.sub: An instruction manual written in four letters, hidden in every one of your cells.

share.v: Your eyes saw my body. In your book they were all written, the days that were ordained for me, when as yet there were none of them.

blocks.h: Inside almost every cell of your body is an instruction manual written in just four letters. The human genome has about 3 billion base pairs. If one book held three million letters, printing it all would fill about 1,000 books.

Stretched out straight, the DNA in a single cell would be about 2 meters long, yet it is neatly packed into a nucleus far smaller than the tip of a pin, and when it is needed, the cell can find exactly the passage it has to read.
Your eyes saw my body. In your book they were all written, the days that were ordained for me, when as yet there were none of them.
A language of four letters

items: Four letters: DNA is made of four bases, A, T, C and G, and the meaning lies in the order in which they are arranged.
Three letters make a word: every three bases form a “codon.” There are 64 of them, corresponding to 20 amino acids plus “stop” signals.
Two complementary strands: A pairs with T and C pairs with G, so each strand is a negative of the other, which makes accurate copying possible.

Reading takes a translation team: the text is first transcribed into RNA, then ribosomes translate it word by word into protein; and the reading machinery itself is built from the instructions in DNA.

blocks.h: DNA is like a recipe book. The paper and ink are chemicals, but how to cook a dish is not found in the chemistry of the ink; it is found in the arrangement of the words. Rearrange the same four letters, and you write an entirely different living thing.

In 1953, James Watson and Francis Crick published their double-helix model of DNA in Nature. Near the end of the paper they remarked, almost in passing, that this pairing immediately suggested a way the genetic material could be copied.

In 2022, an international team published the first complete, gap-free human genome sequence, from telomere to telomere. Scientists can also encode books and images into synthetic DNA and read them back out, showing that DNA is an extraordinarily dense medium for storing information.
DNA is a double helix whose bases pair in complementary fashion, A–T and C–G, allowing genetic information to be copied accurately.
The human genome has about 3 billion base pairs, and the first complete, gap-free sequence was published in 2022.
The genetic code reads bases in groups of three; 64 codons correspond to 20 amino acids plus stop signals.
How much of the non-coding portion of the genome has a function is still being researched and debated.

In our everyday experience, coded information with specific meaning always comes from a mind, so the information in DNA points to an author with a mind. This is a philosophical inference; some scholars hold that information can arise gradually through natural processes.
His wisdom: life is a written text

People write to express what is on their hearts. When we discover that the foundation of life is a language, we cannot help asking: who wrote this text? The Gospel of John tells us from its very first line:
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
All things were made through him. Without him, nothing was made that has been made.
The “Word” is God’s speech. God created the world by speaking, and He also wrote an instruction manual into your cells. You are not a pile of random letters; you are a work written with care.
I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful. My soul knows that very well.
Place your hand on your chest. Right now, tens of trillions of cells in your body are reading, transcribing and translating that manual, without stopping for a moment.
Reflect: The One who wrote the manual for my body has also written His purpose for my life. Am I willing to read the words He has written to me?

Prayer: Lord, Creator of all things, You knew me before I was formed. Thank You for writing my life with wisdom. Please write Your word on the tablet of my heart too, so that I may live according to Your purpose. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: The Bible is my standard: DNA is the manual for the body; the Bible is the manual for life. Only when we live by it does life work the way it should.
Change your mindset, change your life: move from “information” to “revelation,” letting the Holy Spirit light up what you learned today so it becomes knowledge of God.
Let Jesus receive all the glory: my existence is His work, not my own achievement.

blocks.h: This week: read a passage of Scripture each day, copy out one sentence as a “code” written into your life, and try to live it out that same day.
Quiz

quiz.q: How many base “letters” is DNA written with?
quiz.e: Four bases, A, T, C and G; the meaning lies in the order they are arranged.

quiz.q: About how many base pairs are in the human genome?
quiz.e: About 3 billion; the first complete, gap-free sequence was published in 2022.

quiz.q: What kind of statement is “the information in DNA points to an author with a mind”?
quiz.e: It is a philosophical inference drawn from the nature of information (c=4), not a fact directly proven by experiment.

units.title: The Cell: A Miniature City
units.sub: Too small to see, yet like a city with a precise division of labor, running day and night.

share.v: Yahweh, how many are your works! In wisdom, you have made them all. The earth is full of your riches.

blocks.h: A typical human cell is only a fraction of the width of a hair, invisible to the naked eye. Yet step inside and you find a city: walls and gates, a library, power plants, factories, a post office, roads and recycling centers.
This city holds an enormous number of protein molecules, each doing its own job, working without pause.
Yahweh, how many are your works! In wisdom, you have made them all. The earth is full of your riches.
Division of labor in the city

items: Cell membrane = city walls and gates: a lipid bilayer only a few nanometers thick, fitted with channels and pumps that decide who may enter and leave.
Nucleus = central library: it keeps the DNA blueprints and sends out only the page that is needed, copied into RNA.
Mitochondria = power plants: they convert the energy in food into ATP the cell can use.
Endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus = factory and post office: they make and process proteins, then label them with an “address” and ship them out.
Cytoskeleton = road system: microtubules act like highways, with motor proteins carrying cargo along them.
Lysosomes and proteasomes = recycling centers: they break down damaged parts so the materials can be reused.

blocks.h: A cell is like a city not because it matches a city in every detail, but because both face the same challenges: supplies must come in, waste must go out, messages must be passed along, and every department must keep to its post and work with the others.

A newly made protein carries a short “signal sequence” that works like a postal code, determining where in the cell it will be delivered. This discovery won the 1999 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
Cell biologists describe this city in numbers: the size, count and speed of its molecules. Those numbers show us that the cell is crowded but not chaotic; it is a highly ordered system.
The cell membrane is a phospholipid bilayer, and channels and pumps in it selectively control what passes in and out.
Eukaryotic cells contain organelles with different roles, such as the nucleus, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus.
Proteins carry signal sequences that direct them to the correct location.
“The cell is like a city” is a helpful analogy, but the way cells organize themselves is not exactly the same as a human-built city.
The cell’s departments depend on one another and work in coordination, displaying an overall order and purposefulness that points to a wise Designer. This is a philosophical inference.
His wisdom: each part doing its work, helping one another
The Bible’s description of the body of Christ is also a picture of cooperation and shared work:

from whom all the body, being fitted and knit together through that which every joint supplies, according to the working in measure of each individual part, makes the body increase to the building up of itself in love.
No department in the cell is unnecessary, and none can survive on its own. Every part has a place God has arranged:
But now God has set the members, each one of them, in the body, just as he desired.
God’s wisdom is displayed not only in the magnificent starry sky but also in the tiny places we cannot see. He is the God of great things and the God of details.
Look at the palm of your hand. In every square centimeter of skin, thousands upon thousands of these cities are running, and today you have hardly given them a thought.
Reflect: In God’s household, which “department” am I? Have I kept to the place God has given me?

Prayer: God of wisdom, You have ordered even the smallest cell perfectly. Please order my life as well, so that in my family, my church and my workplace I do my part and help others. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Build God’s kingdom system: the cell is a system, and so is the church. Only when each person finds their place can the whole be healthy.
Humility overcomes pride: the mitochondrion does not try to be the nucleus. Return to our proper place: let people be people, and let God be God.
People matter more than tasks: the city runs for the sake of life; ministry is for people, not for the program itself.

blocks.h: This week: find someone who serves quietly in your church or fellowship, thank them, and tell them, “Your place really matters.”
Quiz

quiz.q: Which organelle converts the energy in food into ATP?
quiz.e: The mitochondrion is called the power plant of the cell.

quiz.q: How do proteins get delivered to the right place in the cell?
o: By a signal sequence that works like a postal code
quiz.e: The discovery of signal sequences won a Nobel Prize in 1999.

quiz.q: According to Ephesians 4:16, how does the body grow?
o: Every joint supplies, each part working in its measure
Each member striving on its own
Only the head does the work
quiz.e: “According to the working in measure of each individual part, makes the body increase to the building up of itself in love.”

units.title: Molecular Machines
units.sub: Spinning motors and walking porters, working day and night inside you.

share.v: He is before all things, and in him all things are held together.

blocks.h: Inside your mitochondria are countless tiny rotary motors, each only a few tens of nanometers across. As they spin, they produce ATP, the body’s energy currency.
The ATP you make, use and recycle each day adds up to roughly your own body weight. Most of it is spun out, one molecule at a time, by these motors.
He is before all things, and in him all things are held together.
Three marvelous molecular machines

items: ATP synthase: hydrogen ions flow through a channel in the membrane and turn a rotor; the rotating shaft changes the shape of the head, which joins ADP and phosphate into ATP, like a hydroelectric generator.
Kinesin: it has two “feet” and walks step by step along microtubules, about 8 nanometers per step, using one ATP per step, carrying cargo throughout the cell.

The bacterial flagellar motor: a rotary motor at the base of the E. coli tail, about 45 nanometers across and built from about 20 kinds of parts; it can spin hundreds of times per second and even reverse direction.

blocks.h: ATP synthase is like a watermill: the flowing water (hydrogen ions) turns the waterwheel (rotor), the wheel drives the millstone (head), and the millstone grinds the grain into flour (ATP). Only this mill is so small that a million of them lined up in a row would stretch only about one centimeter.

In 1997, Japanese scientists attached a fluorescent filament to the shaft of the F<sub>1</sub> unit and watched it rotate under a microscope, confirming the rotational catalysis mechanism proposed by Boyer. Boyer received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry that same year.

Using optical tweezers, scientists tracked a single kinesin molecule and saw its “footsteps” as it moved forward. Building and operating the flagellum requires about 40 gene products, assembled in a precise order.
ATP synthase is a rotary motor, and its rotation has been directly observed under the microscope.
Kinesin moves along microtubules in steps of about 8 nanometers.
The bacterial flagellum is driven by a rotary motor that can turn both forward and in reverse.

Whether the flagellum is “irreducibly complex” is a disputed question: Behe argues that it cannot work if any single part is missing, while Pallen, Matzke and others argue that its parts are related to other systems and may have developed gradually.
These molecular machines have engineering features such as motors, shafts and tracks, strongly displaying the appearance of design and pointing to a Designer. This is a philosophical inference.
His wisdom and faithfulness: all things hold together in Him
These machines were not built and then left idle; they are running every second. While you sleep, they keep working. The Bible tells us who is holding all of this together:

For by him all things were created in the heavens and on the earth, things visible and things invisible, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers. All things have been created through him and for him.

His Son is the radiance of his glory, the very image of his substance, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself made purification for our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high.
His faithfulness is in every heartbeat, every breath, every molecule of ATP. He has never stopped holding you up.
Take a deep breath. The oxygen you just breathed in is keeping countless rotary motors turning.
Reflect: Do I often think that I am the one holding my life together?

Prayer: Lord Jesus, all things hold together in You, and so do I. Thank You for holding me up every moment. Teach me to lay down the burdens I try to carry on my own and to trust in Your faithfulness. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Let Jesus reign: all things hold together in Him, so my life should be under His rule too, not propped up by my own straining.
Give thanks in everything: most of grace is unseen. Give the glory to the Lord who holds me up at every moment.
Selflessness: molecular machines do not turn for themselves but for the whole body. It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me.

blocks.h: This week: each night before bed, write down three graces that are “unseen but always at work,” and thank God for them.
Quiz

quiz.q: Which kind of machine is ATP synthase most like?
quiz.e: A flow of ions turns the rotor, which drives the head to make ATP.

quiz.q: About how far does kinesin travel with each step?
quiz.e: Svoboda and colleagues used optical tweezers to observe steps of about 8 nanometers.

quiz.q: According to Hebrews 1:3, how does Christ uphold all things?
o: By the laws of nature themselves
By the word of His power
quiz.e: “Upholding all things by the word of his power.”

units.title: Protein Folding
units.sub: A chain of amino acids folds in an instant into a precise three-dimensional shape.

share.v: But now, Yahweh, you are our Father. We are the clay and you our potter. We all are the work of your hand.

blocks.h: Following the instructions in DNA, the cell links amino acids together one by one into a long chain. But a straight chain can do nothing; it has to fold into a specific three-dimensional shape before it can become an enzyme, an antibody or a part of a muscle.
Many small proteins fold from a tangled thread into the right shape in less than a second, like an origami artist completing a paper crane in an instant.
But now, Yahweh, you are our Father. We are the clay and you our potter. We all are the work of your hand.
From a thread to a work of art

items: Sequence determines shape: the order of the 20 kinds of amino acids determines what shape the protein finally folds into.
Shape determines function: an enzyme’s pocket fits exactly the molecule it acts on, like a key in a lock.
Molecular chaperones: some proteins need “chaperone” proteins beside them to keep them from misfolding or clumping together; some chaperones are like a little room where a protein can fold safely.
Misfolding causes disease: misfolded or clumped proteins are linked to many diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease.

blocks.h: Protein folding is like a strip of paper with the folding instructions already written on it: the creases are hidden in the sequence, and when you let go, it takes shape according to the pattern. Molecular chaperones are like a patient teacher standing by to lend a hand so it does not fold crooked.

Anfinsen found that when ribonuclease was unfolded, it could refold on its own into its original shape, showing that the information for its shape is written in the amino acid sequence. For this he received the 1972 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Levinthal pointed out that if a protein had to try every possible shape one by one, it would take longer than the age of the universe, so folding must follow pathways.

In 2020, DeepMind’s AlphaFold reached near-experimental accuracy in the international protein structure prediction assessment. Half of the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry went to Hassabis and Jumper for protein structure prediction, and the other half to Baker for computational design of new proteins.
A protein’s three-dimensional structure is determined mainly by its amino acid sequence.
Molecular chaperones help many proteins fold correctly and prevent harmful clumping.
AlphaFold can predict protein structure from sequence with high accuracy, and related work received the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
Scientists have theories such as the “energy funnel” to explain how proteins find the right shape so quickly, but the details are still being researched.

Humans need cutting-edge artificial intelligence and massive computing power to predict how a protein will fold, yet cells accomplish it every second; such precision points to a wise Creator. This is a philosophical inference.
His beauty: the Potter’s hands
A protein has to fold into the right shape before it can do its work. Our lives are the same: we need to be shaped by God’s hands to become vessels fit for use.
But now, Yahweh, you are our Father. We are the clay and you our potter. We all are the work of your hand.
Molecular chaperones remind us that God often uses the people around us to walk with us as we are being formed. And God Himself is the Potter who never gives up halfway:
being confident of this very thing, that he who began a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.
For you formed my inmost being. You knit me together in my mother’s womb.
Think back to a recent time when you felt “folded”: perhaps pressure, waiting or brokenness. It may be exactly how God is shaping you.
Reflect: Am I willing to let God fold me into His pattern, or do I insist on keeping my own shape?

Prayer: Father God, my Potter, I am the clay and You are the Potter. Shape me according to Your good pleasure, and send spiritual companions to walk with me as I am formed, so that I may become a vessel fit for the Master’s use. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Life first, then relationships, then ministry: a protein functions only after it has folded. When our lives are shaped first, our service bears fruit.
235 spiritual companions (walking closely with a few others in discipleship): like a molecular chaperone, walk alongside a brother or sister and lend a hand while they are being shaped.
Humility: let God be the Potter and me the clay, returning to our proper place as creatures.

blocks.h: This week: find a spiritual companion, share with each other one way “God is shaping me right now,” and pray for each other.
Quiz

quiz.q: What mainly determines a protein’s three-dimensional shape?
o: The order of its amino acids
quiz.e: Anfinsen’s experiment showed that the information for the shape is written in the sequence.

quiz.q: What do molecular chaperones do?
o: Help proteins fold correctly and avoid clumping
quiz.e: Some chaperones are like a protective little room where a protein can fold properly.

quiz.q: What was the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry awarded for?
quiz.e: Hassabis and Jumper (AlphaFold) and Baker (protein design) shared the prize.

units.title: Where Did Life Come From?
units.sub: One of science’s deepest mysteries, and one of faith’s most fundamental questions.

share.v: For with you is the spring of life. In your light we will see light.

blocks.h: We have already seen that DNA stores information and proteins do the work; yet making proteins requires instructions from DNA, and reading DNA requires proteins. So how did the very first cell come about?
It is a chicken-and-egg puzzle. To this day scientists are still working on it, and there is no agreed answer.
For with you is the spring of life. In your light we will see light.
How scientists explore the question

items: The Miller–Urey experiment (1953): Miller placed water, methane, ammonia and hydrogen in a flask, passed electric sparks through it, and obtained several amino acids, opening the era of experimental origin-of-life research.
A fresh analysis: in 2008 scientists reanalyzed samples Miller had saved and identified 22 amino acids in one of his setups.
The early-atmosphere puzzle: many earth scientists think the early atmosphere may not have been as rich in reducing gases as Miller assumed, which affects what the experiment means.
The RNA world hypothesis: RNA can both store information and catalyze reactions like an enzyme, so perhaps the earliest life used RNA in both roles.

blocks.h: Going from amino acids to a cell is like going from a pile of bricks to a city with electricity, internet, libraries and factories. Getting the bricks is an important step, but the city is still a very long way off.
In 1986, Gilbert coined the term “RNA world.” The later discovery that the catalytic core of the ribosome is RNA lent support to the idea.
The origin-of-life chemist Orgel also acknowledged frankly that synthesizing RNA under non-living conditions, and getting it to copy itself, still faces many unsolved difficulties.

items.h: Many scientists believe life emerged gradually under early-earth conditions through a series of chemical steps. They keep experimenting, hoping to fill in the gaps one step at a time.

Some scholars argue that the coded information and precise systems life requires are best explained as coming from a designer with a mind. This is an inference at the boundary of philosophy and science.
Some Christian scholars hold that even if natural steps are discovered in the future, they would be processes God established and sustains. Whatever the means, God is the source of life.

blocks.h: In 1953, Miller produced amino acids in a spark-discharge experiment.
A 2008 reanalysis of Miller’s saved samples identified 22 amino acids.
The RNA world hypothesis is an important current line of research, but many chemical problems remain unsolved.
How life emerged from non-living chemicals still has no agreed scientific explanation and remains under study.

Life requires information, machines and precise integration, and the best explanation for these appearing together is a life-giving Creator. This is a philosophical inference; scholars who see it differently look to future scientific explanations.
His goodness: life is a gift
Science is still searching for the steps by which life began; the Bible tells us from whom life comes. These are questions on different levels, and they need not be enemies.

The God who made the world and all things in it, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands. He isn’t served by men’s hands, as though he needed anything, seeing he himself gives to all life and breath and all things.
Life is not something we earn; it is something we receive. Deeper still, Jesus gives us not only physical life but eternal life:
In him was life, and the life was the light of men.
Facing unsolved mysteries, we can humbly say, “We don’t know yet.” But about the source of life, we can say with confidence, “It is with You.”
Be still for a moment and notice your breathing and your heartbeat. This life is a gift you have been given.
Reflect: Do I treat my life as my own property, or as a gift received from God?
Prayer: Source of life, my life, my breath and all things are given by You. Let me not merely have physical life, but live the abundant life in Jesus. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Humility overcomes pride: admitting “we don’t know yet” is honesty in science and humility in faith. Let God be God.
People matter more than tasks: when you discuss this with friends who see things differently, respecting them matters more than winning the debate.
From the temporary to the eternal: physical life is limited, but the life Jesus gives lasts forever.

blocks.h: This week: ask a friend, “Where do you think life came from?” Listen first, then gently share why you believe life is a gift from God.
Quiz

quiz.q: What did Miller’s 1953 experiment produce?
quiz.e: Miller obtained amino acids, but that is still a very long way from a cell.

quiz.q: What is the core idea of the RNA world hypothesis?
o: RNA can both store information and catalyze reactions
quiz.e: So RNA might have played the roles of both DNA and enzymes, though many difficulties remain.

quiz.q: Which best describes where science stands on the origin of life today?
o: Still under study, with no agreed explanation
quiz.e: That is the honest situation: research continues, and there is no settled conclusion.

units.title: Wondrous Navigation
units.sub: Butterflies, migratory birds and salmon find a distant home without any map.

share.v: In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.

blocks.h: Every autumn, monarch butterflies from eastern North America fly up to several thousand kilometers to spend the winter in the fir forests of the mountains of central Mexico. Remarkably, the generation that makes the journey has never been there, and their grandparents never came back to show them the way.
Bar-tailed godwits take off from Alaska and fly across the Pacific to New Zealand without eating, drinking or stopping; tracked flights have exceeded 11,000 kilometers.
Yes, the stork in the sky knows her appointed times. The turtledove, the swallow, and the crane observe the time of their coming; but my people don’t know Yahweh’s law.
A built-in compass

items: The monarch’s sun compass: monarchs orient by the sun and use a biological clock in their antennae to correct for the sun’s changing position through the day.
A backup compass for cloudy days: experiments show monarchs can also sense the inclination of Earth’s magnetic field as an aid.
The migratory bird’s magnetic compass: experiments in 1972 confirmed that European robins can sense Earth’s magnetic field to orient themselves.

Salmon coming home: salmon live at sea for years, then return to the river where they were born; up close they recognize their home water by smell, and at sea they may “remember” their birthplace by Earth’s magnetic field.

blocks.h: These animals are like travelers carrying a built-in navigation system: the sun is the compass, a clock corrects the heading, the magnetic field is the backup compass, and smell is the house number for the last mile. No one teaches them, yet it is passed down accurately from generation to generation.

Research found that when the biological clocks in a monarch’s antennae are disrupted, the butterflies fly in the wrong direction. The magnetic compass is an important aid when the sun cannot be seen, such as on cloudy days.

How migratory birds “see” the magnetic field is a hot research topic. One leading hypothesis is that cryptochrome proteins in the eye form radical pairs when struck by light, and these are sensitive to the direction of the magnetic field. A 2021 study showed that cryptochrome 4 from a migratory bird is magnetically sensitive, but the full mechanism has yet to be confirmed.
Monarch butterflies use a time-compensated sun compass, with the clock located in their antennae.
Monarch butterflies also have a light-dependent magnetic compass as a backup.
Migratory birds can orient using Earth’s magnetic field; bar-tailed godwits can fly nonstop across the Pacific.
The molecular mechanism of magnetic sensing in migratory birds (cryptochrome radical pairs) and geomagnetic imprinting in salmon are still under study.
These precise navigation abilities, passed across generations without being learned, point to a Creator who gave His creatures wisdom. This is a philosophical inference.
His wisdom and faithfulness: He will direct your paths
God asked Job:
Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?

Birds know the way home, yet God’s people often lose their way. Jeremiah’s lament is not a rebuke of the birds but a call for people to return. God not only gave animals a compass; He also promises to guide us Himself:
I will instruct you and teach you in the way which you shall go. I will counsel you with my eye on you.
Trust in Yahweh with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
Picture a small monarch taking off in the autumn wind toward a faraway place it has never seen. It does not know the whole route; it only knows which way to fly for the next stretch.
Reflect: Whose compass is my life following right now?

Prayer: God who guides, You lead the butterflies and the birds to find their way home; please guide me too. When I cannot see what lies ahead, help me trust You with all my heart and follow You one step at a time. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: The Holy Spirit is my guide: the monarch relies on its built-in compass; the Christian relies on the leading of the Holy Spirit. Pray and seek Him first in everything.
Lead with a Spirit-led heart, not a self-reliant head: do not lean on your own understanding; trust in Yahweh with all your heart.
Faithfulness: God passes navigation down to His creatures generation after generation, and He leads His people generation after generation.

blocks.h: This week: when you face a decision, stop and pray for five minutes first, then write down the direction you sense.
Quiz

quiz.q: What do monarch butterflies use to correct their sun compass?
o: A biological clock in their antennae
quiz.e: Merlin and colleagues found that the clock is located in the antennae.

quiz.q: Where do bar-tailed godwits fly nonstop to from Alaska?
quiz.e: Tracked flights exceed eleven thousand kilometers, with no stops along the way.

quiz.q: How would you classify the molecular mechanism of magnetic sensing in migratory birds today?
quiz.e: Cryptochrome radical pairs are the leading hypothesis, but the full mechanism has yet to be confirmed.

units.title: After Their Kind: Seeds and the Continuity of Life
units.sub: A tiny seed holds an entire tree and waits for the right time.

share.v: Most certainly I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.

blocks.h: Inside a seed is a tiny embryo and a packed supply of nourishment, all wrapped in a protective seed coat. It can wait quietly for months, years or even longer.
A date seed about 2,000 years old, unearthed by archaeologists at Masada in Israel, was planted in 2005, and it actually sprouted and grew into a date palm.
God said, “Let the earth yield grass, herbs yielding seeds, and fruit trees bearing fruit after their kind, with their seeds in it, on the earth;” and it was so.
The wisdom of seeds

items: A complete package: the embryo is the future plant, the endosperm or cotyledons are its packed lunch, and the seed coat is its armor.
Dormancy: many seeds do not sprout as soon as they ripen; they wait until temperature, moisture or season is right, so they do not pop up at the wrong time.
Germination: the seed absorbs water and swells, the embryo becomes active, and the root goes down first before the shoot comes up.
After their kind: apple seeds grow apple trees and wheat grows wheat; genetic information is passed down faithfully from generation to generation.

blocks.h: A seed is like a sealed letter containing the blueprint of an entire tree, with travel money and armor enclosed. It waits patiently for the moment of delivery, and when the time comes, the letter is opened and the whole tree unfolds from within.
Ancient lotus seeds unearthed from a dried lakebed in northeastern China, radiocarbon dated to about 1,300 years old, were still able to germinate and grow.

Dormancy and germination are regulated by plant hormones: in general, abscisic acid maintains dormancy and gibberellins promote germination, and the balance between them responds to environmental signals.
A seed contains an embryo, nutrient-storage tissue and a seed coat.
A date seed about two thousand years old and lotus seeds over a thousand years old have both successfully germinated.
Dormancy and germination are regulated by hormones and environmental signals; the details vary by species and are still being studied.
The way seeds precisely prepare for, wait for and pass on life reflects the faithfulness and foresight of the Creator. This is a philosophical inference.
His faithfulness: a grain of wheat
After the Flood, God promised:
While the earth remains, seed time and harvest, and cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night will not cease.
Every sowing and every harvest speaks of God’s faithfulness. Jesus also used a seed to explain His own death and resurrection:
Most certainly I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.

A seed must fall into the ground and its outer shell must break open before new life can grow. Jesus gave Himself up, and so bore the fruit of countless saved lives. This is also the path for those who follow Him.
and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should spring up and grow, he doesn’t know how.
You foolish one, that which you yourself sow is not made alive unless it dies.
Hold a seed (a grain of rice, a bean or a fruit pit) in your palm, and think about the whole plant hidden inside it.
Reflect: What in my life needs to “fall into the earth and die” so that God can bring forth more fruit?

Prayer: Faithful Lord, You are the grain of wheat that fell into the earth and laid down Your life for me. Make me willing to deny myself as well, to let my old self die, so that Your life in me may bear much fruit. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Deny yourself: unless a grain of wheat dies, it remains alone. When we lay down our own rights, life multiplies.
Multiplication: the purpose of a seed is to produce more seeds. Pass the gospel and your life on to the next person.
The eight steps of changing our mindset: repetition: a seed needs waiting and watering, and a changed life also needs repeated practice.

blocks.h: This week: plant a bean in a cup and watch how it changes each day, while praying for a friend you want to share the gospel with.
Quiz

quiz.q: What is it called when a ripe seed does not sprout right away?
quiz.e: Dormancy lets a seed wait for the right conditions before sprouting.

quiz.q: About how old was the ancient date seed unearthed at Masada?
quiz.e: It was planted in 2005, sprouted, and grew into a date palm.

quiz.q: According to Jesus, how does a grain of wheat bear much fruit?
o: By falling into the earth and dying
By being stored in a barn
quiz.e: “But if it dies, it bears much fruit.” (John 12:24)

units.title: Completing One Another: Symbiosis and Ecology
units.sub: Figs and wasps, corals and algae, trees and fungi: needing each other and completing one another.

share.v: so we, who are many, are one body in Christ, and individually members of one another.

blocks.h: A fig’s flowers are hidden inside the fruit, where bees and butterflies cannot reach. The only creature that can pollinate them is a fig wasp smaller than a grain of rice.

The female wasp squeezes in through a tiny opening at the tip of the fig, pollinates the flowers and lays her eggs inside; her offspring grow up in the fruit and then fly off carrying pollen. The fig needs the wasp, and the wasp needs the fig.
The eye can’t tell the hand, “I have no need for you,” or again the head to the feet, “I have no need for you.”
Partners who complete one another

items: Figs and fig wasps: of the more than 700 species of figs worldwide, most have their own dedicated pollinating wasp, and neither can reproduce without the other.
Corals and symbiotic algae: tiny algae live inside coral; the algae photosynthesize and supply nutrients, and the coral provides a home and raw materials.
Coral bleaching: when seawater gets too hot, coral expels its symbiotic algae and turns white; if this lasts too long, the coral may die.
Mycorrhizae: the roots of most land plants partner with fungi; the fungi help absorb water and minerals such as phosphorus, and the plants repay them with sugars.

blocks.h: Symbiosis is like a three-legged race: two people have their legs tied together. If each goes their own way, they fall; when they move in step, they can go farther than either could alone.

Researchers have found that although one-to-one pairings of fig wasps and figs are common, there are many exceptions: sometimes one fig species has several wasp species, and sometimes one wasp species serves several fig species.

A 1997 study showed that carbon can be transferred between different trees through underground mycorrhizal networks, sparking the idea of a “wood wide web.” However, a 2023 review pointed out that many claims about “mother trees feeding young trees through the network” have been overinterpreted, and the evidence remains limited.
Figs and fig wasps depend on each other: the wasps pollinate the flowers, and the figs provide a place for the wasps to reproduce.
Reef-building corals partner with symbiotic algae and bleach under heat stress.
Most land plants live in symbiosis with mycorrhizal fungi, exchanging nutrients.
How much common mycorrhizal networks in forests transfer between trees, and what ecological significance they have, is still disputed.
The intricate relationships in which living things complete one another point to a wise Creator who makes all things work together. This is a philosophical inference.
His goodness: needing one another is design, not weakness
The world God designed is not a collection of isolated parts but a web of connections. Job said:

“But ask the animals, now, and they shall teach you; the birds of the sky, and they shall tell you. Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach you. The fish of the sea shall declare to you. Who doesn’t know that in all these, Yahweh’s hand has done this,
God made us the same way: not to live alone, but to complete one another in the body of Christ.
Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.

Having walked through the Life Hall, we see God’s wisdom and goodness everywhere: from the written code of DNA, the city of the cell and molecular motors, to seeds, birds and forests. Paul put it well:

For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, even his everlasting power and divinity, that they may be without excuse.
Think about it: who in your life is like your “symbiotic partner”? What have you received from them, and what have you given them?
Reflect: Do I often think, “I have no need for you”? Am I willing to admit that I need other people?

Prayer: Lord who gives life, thank You for placing me in Your body so that I need not be alone. Make me humble enough to accept help and glad to help others grow, building one another up in love with my brothers and sisters. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: 920 (the fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5:22–23): live the self-emptied life in your relationships and bear the fruit of the Spirit, just as symbiotic partners complete one another.
Relationships matter more than things: our greatest resource is not what we own but who we walk with.
235 comrades in arms (a small band who stand together): find companions to fight alongside you, for a threefold cord is not quickly broken.

blocks.h: This week: write a card to someone who has “completed” you in your life, thank them, and tell them you are praying for them.

Congratulations on completing the Life Hall! From the language of DNA, the city of the cell and molecular machines, to navigating birds, the grain of wheat that falls to the ground and the creatures that complete one another, you have seen God’s wisdom, goodness and faithfulness displayed throughout life, and you have come to know the Lord who gives life and eternal life.
Quiz

quiz.q: What pollinates figs?
quiz.e: A fig’s flowers are hidden inside the fruit, and only fig wasps can get in to pollinate them.

quiz.q: How does coral bleaching happen?
o: Under heat stress, coral expels its symbiotic algae
quiz.e: When the algae leave, the coral turns white, and if this lasts too long, it may die.

quiz.q: Which best describes the claim that “trees feed one another through mycorrhizal networks”?
o: Some effects have evidence, but they are often overinterpreted
quiz.e: A 2023 review cautioned that many claims go beyond the current evidence.

questions.q: Is life a chemical accident, or does it come from a Lord who gives life?
Am I willing to be like a grain of wheat that falls into the earth and dies, so that my life bears much fruit?
